message.content:
**Columbia University**

- **Type:** Private Ivy‑League research university  
- **Location:** Morningside Heights, Manhattan, New York City, New York, USA  
- **Founded:** 1754 (originally King's College) – the oldest institution of higher education in the state of New York  
- **Campus:** Urban, 36 acres (≈ 14 ha) with a mix of historic and modern buildings; main campus is bounded by Broadway, Amsterdam Avenue, 116th Street, and 118th Street.  
- **Student Body:** ~ 32,000 total (≈ 14,000 undergraduates, ≈ 18,000 graduate & professional students)  
- **Academic Structure:** 10 schools and colleges (e.g., Columbia College, Fu Foundation School of Engineering & Applied Science, School of Journalism, School of Law, School of Medicine, School of Social Work, etc.)  
- **Research & Reputation:** Known for strong programs in humanities, social sciences, natural sciences, engineering, journalism, law, medicine, and business. Frequently ranked among the top universities worldwide.  
- **Notable Alumni & Faculty:** Includes 27 Nobel laureates, 5 Turing Award winners, 2 Fields Medalists, 4 Pulitzer Prize winners, 3 U.S. Presidents (Grover Cleveland, Theodore Roosevelt, Franklin D. Roosevelt), and many other prominent scholars, artists, and public figures.  
- **Key Features:**  
  - **Lowell Center** (public policy research)  
  - **Columbia University Libraries** (largest academic library system in the U.S.)  
  - **Theater and Arts:** Columbia University School of the Arts, Columbia Playhouse, and numerous student‑run productions.  
  - **Athletics:** NCAA Division I, Big East Conference; home to the famed “Columbia Lions.”  

For the most up‑to‑date information, you can visit Columbia’s official website at [www.columbia.edu](https://www.columbia.edu).
